blocks.text: A spokesperson for Bell says customers across its network of subsidiaries, including Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile, were affected by a Nov. 17 breach but no "highly sensitive" information such as credit card numbers or banking information was impacted.
Company says no 'highly sensitive' data such as credit card numbers affected in Nov. 17 breach
Bell says customers across its network of subsidiaries, including Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile, were affected by a cybersecurity incident last week.

In an email to CBC News on Monday, a Bell spokesperson said customers with Bell, Bell Aliant, Bell MTS, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile were affected after an "agentic threat actor" accessed some of its internal systems on Nov. 17.
But the company did not say how many customers were impacted.
"We can confirm that no highly sensitive personal information such as credit card numbers or banking information was accessed in the incident," the spokesperson said.
Separately, Virgin Plus sent an email to customers late on Sunday saying "an unknown party" gained access to its internal system on Nov. 17.
Virgin Plus said the incident may have affected some of its customers' personal information — including names, mailing addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and account details.
Virgin Plus also said it continues to monitor all systems closely. "We take our obligation to safeguard your information very seriously and we have engaged the RCMP's cybercrime unit to investigate."
Virgin Plus did not immediately respond to CBC's request for comment Monday morning on how many of its customers were affected.
